newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-HOME FANS CAN BE PROUD OF LIONS-COTTON.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-HOME FANS CAN BE PROUD OF LIONS-COTTON.

text.p: British and Irish rugby has taken a positive step forward after the Lions' 2-1 series defeat of South Africa, the tourists' manager Fran Cotton said on Saturday.
Speaking after the Lions lost the third and final test 35-16, Cotton said: "We lost the test match, but remember that we were 5-1 against to win any of them when we arrived.
"This tour is very important in the development of British and Irish rugby...The whole of Britain and Ireland can be very proud of these players."
Coach Ian McGeechan added: "To come to South Africa when we were written off and to win a series is something special.

"I thought we didn't get out of the game what we deserved (today). We missed chances at 20-9 and 23-16 which proved crucial. But I thought it was a great game and I've congratulated the players on their attitude."
The Lions finished the tough tour with more injuries.
England centre Jeremy Guscott, who clinched the series with a late drop goal in last weekend's second test, fractured his lower arm just before half time. Winger Tony Underwood tore a thigh muscle.
Skipper Martin Johnson regretted not winning the series 3-0 but praised the Springboks for bouncing back from the two defeats to put on an impressive performance on Saturday.
"We had a chance at 23-16 when we were in their 22, but we couldn't control the ball. Last week we took our chances, this week we didn't," he said.
"It just goes to show how well we played in the first two tests, because South Africa are a very good team and they deserved to win today".

"That could have happened in any of the games and it is a tribute to our defence that it didn't until today. The series win is the culmination of a great squad effort in which no single player has let anyone down".
South African coach Carel du Plessis was visibly relieved to have a win under his belt.
"We still lost the series, but this was a very important win. The players were under huge pressure to perform and they did well," he said.
"We were able to get quicker second and third phase ball than was the case in the first two tests and that made space for the backline to perform".
Du Plessis admitted that the South Africans had suffered a great deal because of their poor goal kicking during much of the series.
"I've learned a very important lesson from this series and that is that you have to have a kicker in your team. I still want my teams to score tries, but we need to win test matches," he said.
"You can't let a top level team like the Lions back into the game by not putting points on the board when you are on top".
Du Plessis said he would announce the Springbok squad for the forthcoming Tri-Nations series next Saturday.
Skipper Gary Teichmann will be available despite a bang on the head and a finger in the eye which forced him to leave the field in the second half.
